title: Interfacing a 7-Segment Display with Arduino Uno
subtitle: Displaying Numbers 0–9 Using the Wokwi Simulator
desc: An educational Arduino project demonstrating how a Single Common Cathode 7-Segment Display is interfaced with Arduino Uno to display digits from 0 to 9 using the Wokwi Simulator.
fullDesc: This project demonstrates the interfacing of a Single Common Cathode 7-Segment Display with an Arduino Uno using the Wokwi Simulator. It helps students understand digital outputs, circuit connections, Arduino programming, and display interfacing by displaying numbers from 0 to 9 sequentially. The project is designed for beginners and provides practical exposure to embedded systems and digital electronics without requiring physical hardware.
author: Sujal Prasad

team.name: Anushka Varma
team.role: Project Lead & Embedded Systems Developer (Class IX)

innovation: This project simplifies the understanding of digital display interfacing by using the Wokwi Simulator, allowing students to learn Arduino programming, circuit connections, and embedded systems concepts without requiring physical hardware.
problemStatement: Students often find it difficult to understand how a 7-Segment Display communicates with a microcontroller. Learning digital electronics, Arduino programming, and circuit connections becomes challenging without practical demonstrations.
solutionApproach: The project interfaces a Single Common Cathode 7-Segment Display with an Arduino Uno. Using Arduino digital output pins, individual display segments are controlled to sequentially display digits from 0 to 9. The Wokwi Simulator provides a safe and interactive environment for learning and experimentation.
guide: Connect the 7-Segment Display to the Arduino Uno according to the circuit diagram.
Connect the Common Cathode (COM) pin to GND.
Upload the Arduino program in the Wokwi Simulator.
Observe the display counting from 0 to 9.
Verify that the Decimal Point (DP) remains ON throughout the sequence.
